naslov: NBA Roundup: Doncic nets 45 points in Lakers win
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
Luka Doncic sparked the Los Angeles Lakers en route to a 131–125 victory versus the Toronto Raptors at crypto.com Arena on Sunday.
Continuing his strong start to the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, the Slovenian superstar poured in 45 points. Making 12-of-23 from the field and hitting eight three-pointers, he also finished with 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, and a block in 35 minutes.
Georgian forward Sandro Mamukelashvili added 11 points off the bench for the the team coached by JJ Redick. The visitors played shorthanded. Serbian play-caller Darko Rajakovic lacked interior depth after Austrian Jakob Poeltl was ruled out with a shoulder injury, leaving the team without its starting center.
“I think that this year he came back. He’s in great shape, he looks healthy. And when he’s healthy and when he’s ready to go, he’s just unstoppable,” said 47-year-old Rajakovic in his postgame press conference about facing Doncic. “We were on the body, we had two hands, we had two people on him. We made it as hard as it gets, but he is so big, and he can shoot over anybody on the court.”
Celtics deny German double-doubles
The Boston Celtics defeated the Orlando Magic 108–97 at the Kia Center, overcoming a strong push from Germany’s Tristan da Silva, who posted a double-double consisting of 23 points and 10 rebounds. “We kind of got of kind of got in our own way a little bit, not sticking to to the fundamentals that we want to play with, and making sure that we get a shot off every possession,” said the 24-year-old forward, explaining how his side struggled down the stretch.
Portuguese Neemias Queta and Spanish Hugo Gonzalez started for the C’s, tallying eight and seven points. Bosnian reserve Luka Garza added 12 points, while Great Britain’s Amari Williams did not play. For Orlando, German starter Franz Wagner countered a poor shooting night with a 14-point, 12-assist double-double, Montenegrin Nikola Vucevic had two points, and Georgia’s Goga Bitadze went scoreless.
Traore and Fernandez secure first win
Spanish expert Jordi Fernandez guided the Brooklyn Nets to a 98–90 win against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. French Nolan Traore put in 16 points as a starter. German reserve Moritz Wagner added 14 points, while Israeli Danny Wolf did not see any floor time.
“Moving the ball well, trying to find the best shot every time, and also being consistent on defense,” said 20-year-old Traore, describing what changed to lead to the first win of the year.
“I thought Nolan had great moments, especially in that second half,” added 43-year-old Fernandez. “Everybody contributed, and it was a great win that we needed, obviously.”
Finally, the Golden State Warriors used a strong second half to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124–112, behind Yaxel Lendeborg’s 37 points. Italian Nick Martinelli recorded 10 points and Spain’s Baba Miller scored two for the Clips, but Dutch Malevy Leons remained on the bench for the hosts.
